solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hour of prayer in winter ceremony

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning their join

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A seasonal religious service in winter includes a time set aside for prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Terce is the canonical office said at the third hour of the day, about 9 a.m.

clue.text: Cat on plot getting below ground level?

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing on another sits above it, so the first piece goes on top

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a garden plot or flower bed

explanation.surface: A cat sits on a garden bed, perhaps burying something below the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: someone placed in a tomb lies below ground level.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tombed is to be buried or entombed, placed in a grave under the earth.

clue.text: Month with little energy, mostly quiet

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter of the word for quiet is dropped

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy; little signals an abbreviation
a lull is a quiet period

explanation.surface: A month spent with little energy and mainly in quiet repose.
explanation.definitionFit: Elul is the sixth month of the Jewish civil calendar, falling around August and September.

clue.text: Depression very much evident in bounder

indicators.note: showing up within something means the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: a bounder is an ill-mannered man, a cad
far, as in far better, means very much

explanation.surface: A rotter's low spirits are all too obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very much' sounds like an intensifier in the surface, but it is a synonym in its own right, as in 'far better'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cafard is a French-derived word for low spirits or melancholy, a fit of the blues.

clue.text: Issue of US magazine held up

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting something up makes it read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: Time is a weekly American news magazine

explanation.surface: An edition of an American magazine has been delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue is a verb here, not the magazine number the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or give forth, which is one sense of the verb issue.

clue.text: Knight taken by chess champion in school

indicators.note: one thing taken by another is followed by it, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: Sir Bors is a knight of the Round Table
Mikhail Tal was world chess champion in 1960

explanation.surface: A knight is captured by a grandmaster during a schools chess match.
explanation.walkthrough: Knight suggests N or K, the chess abbreviations; here it is an Arthurian knight. A borstal was a British detention centre for young offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: A borstal was a reform institution for young offenders in Britain, a kind of corrective school.

clue.text: Tree people chucked with Noel finally gone

indicators.note: things chucked about land in a jumble, so the letters are mixed up
gone means removed, so the selected letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the closing letter of the name

explanation.surface: People threw out a Christmas tree once the season ended.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel suggests Christmas and a fir; only its last letter is used, removed from PEOPLE before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Opepe is a West African tree whose yellowish hardwood is used in construction.

clue.text: Pet is quiet with mist falling

parts.note: st! is an interjection calling for silence
roke is a dialect word for mist or smoke; falling places it below in the down entry

explanation.surface: An animal stays quiet while fog comes down.
explanation.walkthrough: Pet is a verb, to caress. Both ST and ROKE are Chambers words that turn up in barred puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet an animal is to stroke it, running a hand gently along its fur.

clue.text: Roman scribe not liable to err

indicators.note: to err is to go astray, so the letters stray from their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An ancient clerk who could not be blamed for any mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabellion was an official notary or scrivener in the Roman empire, drawing up documents.

clue.text: Architectural feature with modern design encompassed by a circle

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something encompassed is surrounded, so it goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a ring is a circle
CAD is computer-aided design

explanation.surface: A building feature with a contemporary look set within a round plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modern design' is the standard abbreviation for computer-aided design, not a style of architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcading is a series of arches, a decorative structural element of buildings.

clue.text: Slip made by you and me after drinks

indicators.note: after means the first-named piece comes second, following the other

parts.note: an animal laps, or drinks, water
us is you and me together

explanation.surface: We made a mistake after a few drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapsus is Latin for a slip or error, as in lapsus linguae, a slip of the tongue.

clue.text: Learned man in house across promenade set back

indicators.note: set back means moved backwards, so the letters read in the opposite direction
lying across something means spanning it, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: HO is the standard abbreviation for house
a mall is a shaded walk or promenade, like the Mall in London

explanation.surface: A scholar lives in a house set back from the promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: An ollamh was a master poet or learned scholar in medieval Ireland, a doctor of learning.

clue.text: Travelling box ripped apart — drug found inside

indicators.note: found inside means placed within the other letters
something ripped is torn up, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A suitcase was torn open and contraband narcotics discovered within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ripped apart' reads as one phrase but splits: ripped is the signal, apart the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A petara is a large box or basket used in India for carrying goods on a journey.

clue.text: Miss at home always is a dish

parts.note: to muff a catch is to miss it
someone at home is in
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A young woman who stays at home is forever a looker.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss looks like a young woman and dish like an attractive person; both are other senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffineer is a covered dish for keeping muffins hot, or a sugar caster for sprinkling them.

clue.text: A sailor with a cold, twitching, gets tranquilliser

parts.note: taken as written
a tar is a sailor
taken as written
C is cold, as on a tap
a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: A seaman with a chill and the shakes is given a sedative.
explanation.definitionFit: An ataractic is a drug that calms the mind, a sedative or tranquillising agent.

clue.text: Drop of rain ultimately bothers pussy?

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the closing letter of the next word counts

parts.note: the closing letter of the word
a pussy cat is a typical pet, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: In the end a raindrop annoys the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Spet is a Scots word for a drop or small fall of rain.

clue.text: Bits of foreign money are collected by little members

indicators.note: things collected are gathered up within, so the short piece goes inside

parts.note: toes are small limbs, little members of the body
A is the symbol for an are, a metric unit of area

explanation.surface: Small coins from abroad are gathered by tiny hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' does double duty in the indicator but also supplies A, the unit of area of 100 square metres.
explanation.definitionFit: The toea is a coin of Papua New Guinea, a hundredth of a kina; these are several of them.

clue.text: Desperate to move, having to abandon area denuded of trees?

indicators.note: to move the letters is to rearrange them
abandoning something means leaving it out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious to relocate after being forced to leave a deforested region.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrepe is a legal term for laying waste land, as by felling its trees, so estreped land is stripped.

clue.text: Form of martial art Hans took up

indicators.note: taken up in the sense of stirred up or disturbed, the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Hans has taken up a fighting sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took up' reads as a phrasal verb; up is the only signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Shotokan is a widely practised style of karate, founded by Gichin Funakoshi.

clue.text: Relevant vision ace brought to the fore

indicators.note: moving something to the front means it now leads the word

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
a dream is a vision

explanation.surface: A pertinent insight from a top performer is put first.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of DREAM moves from its fourth place to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad rem is Latin for 'to the matter', meaning to the point or pertinent.

clue.text: Anthropologist enthusiastic about first bit of evidence

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: mad about something is enthusiastic about it

indicators.note: the first bit of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A researcher gets keen at the first hint of proof.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Mead was a celebrated American anthropologist, author of Coming of Age in Samoa.

clue.text: Pear mum cut the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means reading backwards
cut means trimmed, so the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: mum, as in keep mum, means silent

explanation.surface: Mother sliced the fruit badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum looks like mother but means saying nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelis is a variety of winter pear, short for Winter Nelis.

clue.text: Fish near danger, avoiding current

parts.note: to can mean near, as in close to

indicators.note: avoiding something means leaving it out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a risk is a danger
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Fish close to peril keep out of the stream.
explanation.definitionFit: The torsk is a North Atlantic fish of the cod family, also called the cusk.

clue.text: Like cannelloni in food container getting devoured

parts.note: a tub is a container, as for ice cream or margarine
ate is devoured, past tense

explanation.surface: Pasta in a carton gets gobbled up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubate means tubular or tube-shaped, as cannelloni pasta tubes are.

clue.text: Jock's firm, so compassionate, not half

indicators.note: not half means only half is kept, so the back half of the word goes

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus
caring means compassionate

explanation.surface: A Scottish company is kind, though not hugely so.
explanation.walkthrough: Firm looks like a business but is the adjective meaning secure; Jock signals Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Siccar is a Scots form of sicker, meaning firm, sure or secure.

clue.text: A hat, one old award to be returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
aret is a Spenserian verb meaning to award or adjudge

explanation.surface: A hat and an old prize are being sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: A terai is a wide-brimmed felt hat with a double crown, worn in hot climates.

clue.text: Fine fellows in port abandoning navy

indicators.note: in means placed within the other piece
abandoning something means leaving it behind, so that letter goes

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen
N is the abbreviation for navy
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Sailors in harbour pay a penalty after deserting the fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine is a noun, the penalty, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An amende is a penalty or fine, from the French, as in amende honorable.

clue.text: Ivy can be explosive, dear, when upset

parts.note: HE is high explosive

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tells a dear friend that Ivy can be volatile when annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivy looks like a woman's name; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedera is the botanical genus name of ivy, the climbing evergreen plant.

clue.text: Alarm about cat in fight once

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a scare is an alarm
a mog or moggy is a cat

explanation.surface: Panic around a cat caught in a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: Once marks an archaic word; Spenser uses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarmoge is an old Spenserian form of skirmish, a brief fight.

clue.text: Bit of old armour fashioned to protect artist

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the second piece goes inside

parts.note: cut means shaped or fashioned
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A piece of ancient armour was made to guard a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A curat is an old word for a cuirass, the breastplate of a suit of armour.

clue.text: A Conservative nut seen in retrospect as a mug

indicators.note: retrospect means looking back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a cob is a hazelnut

explanation.surface: A Tory crank is later judged to have been a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Mug is slang for face or mouth, not a fool or cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Bocca is Italian for mouth, and mug is slang for the face or mouth.

clue.text: Deposit five hundred away from city

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun for one kind of sediment

indicators.note: away from means taken out of, so the numeral is removed

parts.note: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Someone pays a deposit of 500 while away from town.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the sediment that settles in a wine bottle or cask, a deposit.

clue.text: Poet's once more taking time over noun

indicators.note: in a down clue over means above, so the first piece sits on top

parts.note: an age is a long time
N is the grammatical abbreviation for noun

explanation.surface: A writer once again takes ages over a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: Agen is an archaic poetic spelling of again, meaning once more.

clue.text: Ship repair brings trouble and anger, not right

parts.note: care is worry or trouble

indicators.note: not right means the letter for right is dropped

parts.note: to enrage is to anger
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Fixing a boat causes worry and fury, which is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Anger is a verb here, giving ENRAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Careenage is the careening of a ship, tilting it to clean or repair its hull, or the place or fee for this.

clue.text: Staff given fish — what a surprise!

parts.note: the tai is a Japanese sea bream
aha is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Employees are handed fish, to their astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff means a weapon, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A taiaha is a Maori fighting staff of hardwood, also used ceremonially.

clue.text: More revolutionary, even after revolution

parts.note: a word that is unchanged when turned end to end, reading the same in both directions

explanation.surface: Someone becomes more radical still once the uprising is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the whole word turned round: it spells the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a byword for left-wing revolutionary, so the comparative means more extreme in that politics.

clue.text: Chaps losing head with foxy female lacking self-control

indicators.note: losing its head means the opening letter is removed
lacking means without, so the named letter is removed

parts.note: chaps are men
foxy means cunning or crafty
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Men falling for a seductive woman show no restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking self-control' reads as a phrase, but lacking belongs to the wordplay and self-control alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Encraty is a rare word for self-restraint or temperance, from Greek enkrateia.

clue.text: Plant, something brownish-yellow I uprooted

indicators.note: something uprooted is pulled out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: sienna is a brownish-yellow pigment
taken as written

explanation.surface: A yellowish-brown plant was pulled up by me.
explanation.definitionFit: Senna is a cassia plant whose dried pods and leaves are used as a laxative.
